bc.title: Performing Fire — The Broadcast
bc.footer.tagline: Y = f(X) + ε · MOST SYSTEMS REDUCE ε. WE PERFORM IT.
bc.about.1.label: 01 / EQUATION
bc.about.1.heading: Y = f(X) + ε
bc.about.1.body: X is what people bring. f(X) is the system's attempt to organize it. ε is what will not stay put.
bc.about.2.label: 02 / INPUT
bc.about.2.heading: X / TRACES
bc.about.2.body: People bring messages, voices, drawings, gestures, movements, hopes, fears, and short videos. These traces are X: the raw material.
bc.about.3.label: 03 / MAP
bc.about.3.heading: f(X) / THE MAP
bc.about.3.body: The proposed system embeds, clusters, and maps the traces. f(X) is its attempt to make them legible and manageable.
bc.about.4.label: 04 / REMAINDER
bc.about.4.heading: ε / WHAT RESISTS
bc.about.4.body: Mistranslations, contradictions, silence, strange gestures, and unclear signals resist the map. Most AI systems reduce ε. Here, we perform it.
bc.about.5.label: 05 / PERFORMANCE
bc.about.5.heading: THE REMAINDER BURNS
bc.about.5.body: A performer works inside or around the fabric totem, changing ε into light, particles, sound, glitch, and symbolic fire.
bc.contribute.1.label: 01 / WHAT TO SEND
bc.contribute.1.heading: LEAVE A TRACE
bc.contribute.1.body: Send a question, hope, fear, or imagination about technology. The text form is live; voice and video are interface studies and do not upload media.
bc.contribute.2.label: 02 / WHAT HAPPENS
bc.contribute.2.heading: TRACE → MAP → ε
bc.contribute.2.body: Your trace joins the work's input. The proposed pipeline maps it; what resists that map becomes material for performance.
bc.contribute.3.label: 03 / CONSENT
bc.contribute.3.heading: BEFORE TRANSMISSION
bc.contribute.3.note: SUBMISSIONS WAIT FOR MODERATION BEFORE PUBLICATION
bc.contribute.4.label: 04 / RECEIVED
bc.contribute.4.heading: ARTIST RESPONSES
bc.contribute.5.label: 05 / SEND
bc.contribute.5.heading: YOUR OFFERING
bc.experiments.1.label: 01 / BROADCAST OBJECTS
bc.experiments.1.heading: CANDLE TV · RACK B
bc.experiments.1.body: Slabs and an Open Frame test a modular wall: one signal, many repeatable containers.
bc.experiments.2.label: 02 / WATER STUDY
bc.experiments.2.heading: FALL / COLLIDE / BREAK
bc.experiments.2.body: Water falls, collides, and breaks. Motion becomes the thing the container has to hold.
bc.experiments.3.label: 03 / CAMERA + DATA
bc.experiments.3.heading: CHEOMSEONGDAE / JANGSEUNG
bc.experiments.3.body: A Cheomseongdae camera, a satellite dish, and a data jangseung turn looking into a broadcast object.
bc.experiments.4.label: 04 / MOON JARS
bc.experiments.4.heading: HOLDING SIGNAL
bc.experiments.4.body: Moon jars keep the field quiet: a container for light, memory, and the next transmission.
bc.experiments.5.label: 05 / STUPA FORMS
bc.experiments.5.heading: TOTEM → STUPA
bc.experiments.5.body: Ceramic, wind, jewel, and vertical celadon studies move the totem toward a stackable form.
bc.research.1.label: 01 / NJP CORPUS
bc.research.1.heading: STUDYING THE SOURCE FIELD
bc.research.1.body: The corpus starts with Nam June Paik Art Center records, video-archive metadata, the official video library, official YouTube metadata, and an ANTIEGG Fluxus reference. We study how broadcast, machines, bodies, and modular systems become material.
bc.research.2.label: 02 / READING
bc.research.2.heading: SIGNAL / MACHINE / BODY
bc.research.2.body: NJP's work is a prompt to read transmission as form: screens, relay, repetition, interruption, and the body in the loop.
bc.research.3.label: 03 / REFERENCE FIELD
bc.research.3.heading: CONTAINERS + RITUAL
bc.research.3.body: TV slabs, racks, dishes, data totems, moon jars, stupa forms, and a cyberpunk columbarium are visual references—not a catalogue, but a field for testing what can hold a signal.
bc.research.4.label: 04 / CORPUS RULE
bc.research.4.heading: METADATA FIRST
bc.research.4.body: The corpus stays rights-aware: public source records and factual metadata first, with raw media held outside the repo. It is a research instrument, not a finished model.
bc.research.5.label: 05 / RESPONSE REEL
bc.research.5.heading: A SEED REEL
bc.research.5.body: Twelve anonymous responses from 2026-07-22: seven in English, five in Korean, spanning painting, sound art, curation, media art, choreography, writing, photography, ceramics, poetry, composition, translation, and film. The archive asks machines to forget, hesitate, and disagree; it is a seed reel, not a representative result.
bc.log.1.label: PROPOSED · 07/07–18
bc.log.1.heading: THEME + CONCEPT
bc.log.1.body: The proposed schedule opens with theme development, the mission debrief, roles, and concept refinement.
bc.log.2.label: PROPOSED · 07/19–25
bc.log.2.heading: RESEARCH + RESPONSE
bc.log.2.body: Detailed research, artist response study, and a multimodal microsite test for text, voice, and video.
bc.log.3.label: PROPOSED · 07/26–08/08
bc.log.3.heading: STRUCTURE + PROTOTYPE 1
bc.log.3.body: Structure, the AI Score workflow, fire visuals, and the first text → Score → visual interaction test.
bc.log.4.label: PROPOSED · 08/09–22
bc.log.4.heading: PROTOTYPE 2 + INTEGRATION
bc.log.4.body: Textile and projection mapping lead into an integration test, feedback, and Phase 2 planning.
bc.log.5.label: PROPOSED · 08/23–31
bc.log.5.heading: RESULTS + REPORT
bc.log.5.body: Results, the Phase 2 development plan, and final report review close the project window.
